skill.name: full-output-enforcement
skill.description: Enforces complete AI responses by banning placeholder shortcuts, requiring all requested deliverables, and defining clear continuation behavior for long outputs.
skill.summary: Helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce complete, placeholder-free outputs.
skill.author: leonxlnx

security_audit.summary: The two static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks used for inline examples and a fenced pause marker in SKILL.md. No executable code, command invocation, network access, secret access, or prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed file.

static_findings.snippet: **In code blocks:** `// ...`, `// rest of code`, `// implement here`, `// TODO`, `/* ... */`, `// si

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 16 uses Markdown inline backticks to list banned placeholder strings inside prose. It does not define or execute a shell command.
Lines 37-39 are a Markdown fenced block showing a pause marker for long responses. No executable code or command invocation is present.

content.value_statement: AI assistants often omit code or compress repeated sections. This skill forces complete deliverables, bans placeholder shortcuts, and defines clean continuation behavior for long outputs.
actual_capabilities: Instructs the assistant to count requested deliverables before answering.
Bans placeholder code comments and omitted-section markers.
Requires full implementations instead of skeletons when full work is requested.
Defines a clean pause marker for token-limit splits.
Requires a final cross-check against the original request.
limitations: Cannot expand the model context window or token budget.
May produce longer responses than needed for small tasks.
Does not validate generated code by running tests.
Can conflict with tasks where the user explicitly wants concise output.

use_cases.title: Generate complete implementation files
use_cases.description: Request full files or component sets without omitted middle sections or placeholder comments.

use_cases.title: Prepare exhaustive technical content
use_cases.description: Create long documentation sections where every requested topic must be completed.

use_cases.title: Audit response completeness
use_cases.description: Check that an AI response includes every requested deliverable before it is accepted.

prompt_templates.title: Complete Single Deliverable
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one finished output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use full-output-enforcement. Produce the complete [deliverable] for [goal]. Include every requested section and avoid placeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Multiple Finished Items
prompt_templates.prompt: Use full-output-enforcement. Create [number] complete deliverables for [project]. Before finishing, verify that all [number] items are present.

prompt_templates.title: Long Output With Continuation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request likely to approach token limits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use full-output-enforcement. Write the full result for [large task]. If you approach the token limit, stop only at a clean breakpoint and wait for continue.

prompt_templates.title: Completeness Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing AI answer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use full-output-enforcement. Compare this response against the original request. List any missing deliverables, placeholders, or compressed sections.

output_examples.input: Create five onboarding email sections for a product launch.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns all five named sections with complete copy and no note that similar sections were omitted.

output_examples.input: Generate a full dashboard component set for a product team.
output: A pause marker appears only if the response reaches a token limit.

best_practices: Use it when the request needs complete files, repeated structures, or exhaustive lists.
State the expected number of deliverables before asking for a long output.
Use continue only when the response pauses at a clean breakpoint.
anti_patterns: Using it for short answers where brevity is more valuable than completeness.
Treating it as a substitute for tests, review, or compilation.
Combining it with prompts that demand summaries or intentionally partial drafts.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It tells the assistant to provide complete outputs and avoid placeholder shortcuts.

faq.question: Does it make responses longer?
faq.answer: Yes. It favors complete deliverables over concise summaries when the task requires full output.

faq.question: Can it bypass token limits?
faq.answer: No. It cannot expand token limits, but it defines how to pause and continue cleanly.

faq.question: Is it useful for code generation?
faq.answer: Yes. It is useful when you need full files, complete functions, or repeated implementation patterns.

faq.question: Does it run commands or modify files?
faq.answer: No. The skill is prompt-only and contains no executable scripts.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it when you need a brief answer, a summary, or an intentionally partial draft.
